newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen tightens control of out-of-town brokers.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen tightens control of out-of-town brokers.

text.p: Shenzhen authorities have tightened supervision over brokerages from the other parts of China to improve risk control in the financial markets, the Shenzhen-based Securities Times said on Wednesday.
A circular issued by the Shenzhen branch of the People's Bank of China, the central bank, has said all out-of-town brokerages must be subsidiaries of securities houses and trust and investment firms.
The brokerages must submit to the central bank branch balance sheets and profit and loss statements each month, the circular said. They must also provide written annual business reports to the bank.
They must not lease the brokerages and trading seats to other companies and must not set up unapproved subordinate offices, the circular said.
Each brokerage must have a general manager and a deputy and they must be empowered by their parent firm, it said.
Violaters will be punished in accordance with securities rules, the circular said but gave no details.
